solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fast runner in leading position backed, covered by stake

indicators.note: covered by says the backed piece sits wrapped inside the word for a stake

parts.note: an ante is the stake put up before a poker hand

indicators.note: backed means the word for the leading position is read from its end to its start

parts.note: pole position is the front place on a starting grid

explanation.surface: A sprinter who has taken the lead turns out to have been staked by gamblers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast runner' suggests an athlete but is an animal; 'backed' flips the grid term to ELOP and 'covered by' wraps the poker stake round it.
explanation.definitionFit: The animal named is a type of very swift grazing beast of the African plains, a classic example of a fast runner.

clue.text: Incorrectly rank hat as lambskin

indicators.note: Incorrectly says the letters of the hat phrase are set in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Someone wrongly grades a hat as being made of sheepskin.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the curly fleece of young Karakul lambs, a type of lambskin used for hats and coats.

clue.text: Land fish: is one going to tuck in?

indicators.note: going to tuck in says the is-and-one pair is placed inside the fish word

parts.note: the tuna is a large sea fish
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone lands a fish and asks if anyone will eat it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Land fish' looks like a verb and object, but 'Land' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a North African country, and a country is a land.

clue.text: Speaker's cat catching a rook

definitions.note: the clue means the speaker's organ, the voice box

indicators.note: catching says the cat word grabs the a-and-rook pair inside it

parts.note: the lynx is a wild cat
R is the chess notation for rook

explanation.surface: A speaker's pet cat catches a rook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speaker's' stands for a speaker's organ, the voice box.
explanation.definitionFit: The voice box holds the vocal cords, so it is the organ belonging to any speaker.

clue.text: God, number one of that name? I believe in them all

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild
The is the title of a clan chief, as in The Macnab, meaning the head of that name
1ST, first, is written IST

explanation.surface: Someone declares belief in a god, chief of his kind, and all others too.
explanation.walkthrough: A Scottish clan chief is styled 'The', as in The Mackintosh, meaning chief of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who worships all gods, or sees the deity in everything, could say they believe in every one.

clue.text: Endlessly put off covering a mark and smear

indicators.note: covering says the shortened word goes round the a-and-mark pair
Endlessly says the word for put off loses its final letter

parts.note: to defer is to postpone or put off
M is short for mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: Someone keeps postponing things while hiding a stain and spreading slander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' cuts DEFER to DEFE, which by 'covering' wraps round A and M.
explanation.definitionFit: To smear someone is to damage their reputation with false claims, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Coupling a disadvantage as pair finally go for run

indicators.note: the final pair of letters goes and is swapped for the run letter

parts.note: a drawback is a disadvantage
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A railway link is a weak point as a couple finally leave to sprint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as pair finally go for' replaces the last two letters, CK, of DRAWBACK with R.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the bar on a tractor or locomotive used to hitch on a trailer, a type of coupling.

clue.text: Outlaw's skill: poultry beheaded at end of day

indicators.note: at end of says the skill and poultry pieces come after the day

parts.note: FRI is short for Friday
art is skill

indicators.note: beheaded says the poultry word loses its first letter

parts.note: a duck is a farmyard fowl

explanation.surface: An outlaw shows his skill by cooking a headless fowl at nightfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beheaded' cuts DUCK to UCK.
explanation.definitionFit: The jolly friar was one of Robin Hood's band of outlaws in Sherwood Forest.

clue.text: Shark not female, like 6

indicators.note: not says the female letter is absent from the shark name

parts.note: the monkfish, or angel shark, is a kind of shark

explanation.surface: A shark that is not female is compared to the outlaw friar.
explanation.definitionFit: The outlaw friar is a religious brother, so anything like him is like a member of a religious order.

clue.text: Without yen, very little money

indicators.note: Without says the yen letter is dropped from the word for very little

parts.note: tiny means very little
Y is the symbol for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: Having no Japanese currency leaves a traveller with hardly any cash.
explanation.walkthrough: TIN is old British slang for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: In dated British slang a stash of cash is called tin, so it is a slang synonym.

clue.text: Architect listened to great applause for modernising

indicators.note: listened to says the architect's name counts as it is heard, with its silent first letter gone

parts.note: Sir Christopher Wren was the architect of St Paul's Cathedral
an ovation is a burst of great applause

explanation.surface: An architect heard rapturous clapping for his updating of a building.
explanation.walkthrough: WREN spoken sounds like REN, the W being silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Renovation is the act of updating or restoring a building, so it is modernising work, a noun sense of the gerund.

clue.text: Jacks in the drink: it's bitter

parts.note: jacks are sailors, and AB (able seaman) is the usual crossword sailor, so ABS

explanation.surface: Sailors who have ended up overboard find the sea water bitter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the drink' reads as fallen into the sea, but 'drink' starts the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The green wormwood spirit is famously a bitter-tasting alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Playwright pulling back from boundary

indicators.note: pulling back from says the back letter of the boundary word is drawn off

parts.note: a barrier is a boundary or fence

explanation.surface: A dramatist withdraws from a line he will not cross.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulling back' means removing the back, the final R.
explanation.definitionFit: J. M. Barrie was the Scottish dramatist who wrote Peter Pan, so he is a playwright.

clue.text: Was told to ignore Resistance leader

indicators.note: to ignore says the resistance letter is left out of the word for was told

parts.note: heard means was told
R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A wartime partisan chief was instructed to disregard orders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resistance leader' reads as a French partisan chief, but Resistance gives only R.
explanation.definitionFit: A head is the person in charge, such as a head of department, a straight synonym for leader.

clue.text: Walk quietly up, skirting unusual threat from this?

definitions.text: Walk quietly up, skirting unusual threat from this?

indicators.note: skirting says the turned walking word runs round the jumbled letters
up in a down clue says the walking word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: to pad is to walk softly

indicators.note: unusual says the letters of threat are put in a strange order

explanation.surface: Someone creeps up softly, edging round an odd danger, perhaps a fatal one.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' flips the walking word to DAP; 'unusual' scrambles threat to EATHTR and 'skirting' wraps DAP round it. Read whole, the clue pictures someone tiptoeing past a lethal hazard.
explanation.definitionFit: A hazard you might sneak past cautiously, hoping to avoid a fatal danger, is a fitting description of it.

clue.text: In drink, German is beside himself

indicators.note: In says the German word goes inside the word for drink

parts.note: a draught is a swallow of drink
ist is German for is

explanation.surface: A German man who has had a drink is wildly upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone beside himself is frantic with worry or grief, an idiom matching the adjective.

clue.text: Losing footing, go down hard on board? It's not beyond repair

indicators.note: Losing footing says the foot, the last letter in a down clue, is dropped

parts.note: to tread on something is to step hard on it
a table is a board, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: Someone slips, falls heavily on the deck, and is told the injury can be fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the footing is the bottom letter, so TREAD loses D.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can be dealt with or cured is not past repair.

clue.text: Tickle bird, badly worried

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
ill means badly, as in ill-treated
ate means worried, as in what's eating you

explanation.surface: Someone tickles a bird which is upset and fretting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' looks like an anagram signal; it is ILL.
explanation.definitionFit: To excite or arouse pleasantly is close to the figurative sense of tickle, as in tickle one's fancy.

clue.text: Conjuror's rueful remark, losing his stick occasionally?

definitions.text: Conjuror's rueful remark, losing his stick
definitions.meaning: a magician who has mislaid his wand might sigh that he then had none
from time to time, at intervals

explanation.surface: A magician ruefully remarks on mislaying his wand, as happens every so often.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as NO WAND THEN, it is the conjuror's complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means from time to time, a fixed idiom for something happening at irregular intervals.

clue.text: Commander right about alternative to Hamlet, period

indicators.note: about says the commander and right letters go round the Hamlet phrase

parts.note: OC is short for officer commanding
Hamlet weighs to be against not to be, so the alternative is to be

explanation.surface: A commanding officer quibbles with Hamlet's famous dilemma over a time span.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet's soliloquy begins 'To be, or not to be'.
explanation.definitionFit: It names the tenth month, which is a period of the calendar.

clue.text: Too dry and hot unfortunately for visitor to Oz

indicators.note: unfortunately says the letters are set in a poor order

parts.note: H is short for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: An Australian holidaymaker complains of an excessively arid and baking climate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oz' suggests Australia, but it is the Land of Oz.
explanation.definitionFit: The heroine of The Wizard of Oz, blown there from Kansas, is a visitor to that land.

clue.text: Bird's tight feeling in stomach?

definitions.meaning: a small wading bird of the sandpiper family has this name
a clench of nerves felt in the belly, as in a nervous lump in the gut

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher feels nervous tension in their gut.
explanation.definitionFit: It names both a wading shorebird and the tight knotted sensation of nerves in one's gut.

clue.text: Part of prison: a cell extended for engine casing

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A section of a jail has a cell enlarged to house an engine.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition included 'for', a link word: 'for engine casing' cannot replace a noun, so the definition is 'engine casing' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the streamlined housing for an aircraft engine, a casing that encloses the motor.

clue.text: Practise fighting soldiers: no comfort here

parts.note: to spar is to practise boxing
TA is the Territorial Army

explanation.surface: Soldiers train at combat in a place with no luxuries.
explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army (TA) is Britain's volunteer reserve force.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek city-state was famed for austere living, hence the word spartan, so it offered no comfort.

clue.text: User of acid as anaesthetic about to be arrested

indicators.note: to be arrested says the about letter is held inside the anaesthetic

parts.note: ether was an early anaesthetic
C is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: A drug user taking acid as a painkiller is about to be nicked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'User of acid' suggests LSD; it is an artist who bites a plate with acid.
explanation.definitionFit: An engraver who makes prints by corroding metal plates with acid is a user of acid.

clue.text: Unlike you, in play I act badly

indicators.note: badly says the letters of the play phrase are put in poor order

explanation.surface: An actor tells someone that in this production he performs poorly, unlike them.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unusual or out of character, as one might be unlike oneself, so unlike you means not typical.

clue.text: In the shade, running water and glass that's got left out

parts.note: a burn is a Scottish stream

indicators.note: got combines with out to say a letter has been taken away
out says the left letter is removed from the glass word

parts.note: a tumbler is a drinking glass

explanation.surface: In the shade, someone has a stream and a glass, but something has been left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got ... out' removes L from TUMBLER, giving TUMBER; a BURN is a Scottish word for a stream.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a dark reddish-brown pigment, a particular shade or colour used by painters.

clue.text: Grassy area is a little piece of greenery short

indicators.note: short says the word for the bit of greenery loses its final letter

parts.note: a leaf is a small bit of a plant's greenery

explanation.surface: A patch of lawn is just a scrap of green, too small.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetic word for a meadow or open grassland, so a grassy area.

clue.text: Go round one place several times

indicators.note: round says the attempt word goes about the one-and-place pair

parts.note: a go is a try or attempt
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone circles a spot over and over again.
explanation.definitionFit: It means three times over, a particular number of times, hence several times.

clue.text: Jargon on lease reinterpreted

parts.note: on is the leg side in cricket

indicators.note: reinterpreted says the letters of the word lease are given a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Specialist language in a tenancy agreement has been read a different way.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on side is also called the leg side, the half of the field behind the batter's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the impenetrable specialised language of lawyers, a kind of professional jargon.
